findings.evidence: Simple.lean:264-271 — the `a ≠ i` branch is `(isZero_simpleRep_obj ha).eq_of_src _ _` (no hypothesis); the `b ≠ i` branch uses `hM` only to make both sides zero, which `M.map p x = 0` already gives; the `b = i` branch uses `hQ.eq_nil` only to avoid `Sᵢ.map p = 0` (Simple.lean:173 `simpleRep_map_eq_zero_of_length_ne_zero`). Compare `indecProjRepHom` (Projective/Basic.lean:191), which takes an arbitrary `x` with no side conditions.
findings.fix: Restate as `noncomputable def simpleRepHom {i : Q} {M : QuiverRep k Q} (x : M.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj i)) (hx : ∀ {b : Q} (p : Quiver.Path i b), p.length ≠ 0 → M.map p x = 0) : simpleRep k Q i ⟶ M`, dropping `hQ` and `hM` (equivalently take `hx` arrow-wise, via `Quiver.Path.eq_toPath_comp_of_length_eq_succ`). In `exists_iso_simpleRep_of_simple`, supply `hx` from `h1`: `M.map p x ∈ pathImages x 1 b` by `Submodule.subset_span`, and `h1 b` says that span is `⊥`.
findings.issue: `simpleRepHom` takes both `hQ : Quiver.IsAcyclic Q` and `hM : ∀ a ≠ i, IsZero (M.obj a)`; neither is needed. Naturality at `a ≠ i` uses only `isZero_simpleRep_obj`; the cases `a = i` (with `b = i` or `b ≠ i`) reduce, via `simpleRep_map_eq_zero_of_length_ne_zero`, to `M.map p x = 0` for positive-length `p`. As stated the definition — and `simpleRepHom_app_generator` — is unusable outside its single call site, instead of being the description of `Hom (Sᵢ) M`.

findings.evidence: Subrepresentation.lean:232 `rw [hQ.eq_nil p]` with `p : Quiver.Path i i`; Subrepresentation.lean:244 `rw [hQ.length_eq_zero p]` with `p : Quiver.Path i i`. `pathSpan_zero_eq_pathSpan_one_of_ne` (line 215) already needs no acyclicity, and the classification (Simple.lean:307-336) invokes `hQ` only through these two lemmas and `simpleRepHom`, all at the single vertex `i`.
findings.fix: Replace `hQ : Quiver.IsAcyclic Q` in both by `(h : ∀ p : Quiver.Path i i, p = Quiver.Path.nil)` (proofs unchanged modulo `h p`), and rename accordingly. With finding 1 this also localises the classification: `Simple M → ¬IsZero (M.obj i) → (∀ p : Quiver.Path i i, p = Quiver.Path.nil) → Nonempty (M ≅ simpleRep k Q i)`, with the roadmap-pinned `exists_iso_simpleRep_of_simple` a two-line corollary (`hQ.eq_nil`).
findings.issue: `pathSpan_zero_self_of_isAcyclic` (line 228) and `pathSpan_one_self_of_isAcyclic` (line 240) assume acyclicity of the whole quiver but apply it only to closed paths at the base vertex `i` (`hQ.eq_nil p` and `hQ.length_eq_zero p` for `p : Quiver.Path i i`). The hypothesis is strictly stronger than the proof uses, so the results say nothing at a cycle-free vertex of a quiver with cycles elsewhere.

summary: `simpleRepHom` assumes global acyclicity of `Q` and vanishing of `M` away from `i`, when the naturality square only needs `x` to be annihilated by the positive-length paths out of `i`; the two `pathSpan` acyclicity lemmas likewise use `hQ` only at the single vertex `i`.
